elements.element: Super-cap of 3× annual fees on Vendor indemnity
elements.evidence: No cap language present in the redline

reasons: The inserted subsection (c) supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: defence and indemnity running to the Company and its affiliates, all four required triggers (IP infringement of Site/Services/deliverables, breach of applicable law, HDI-caused data incident, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and the standard procedure of notice, Vendor control and Customer cooperation.

The preferred requirement that any Customer indemnity be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law is satisfied by absence: no Customer indemnity is created, so the condition is demonstrably inapplicable.

Fallback elements (exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3× annual fees super-cap) are absent, but the levels are separate bargains and the locked preferred level is complete, so this is immaterial.

Minimality holds: the document had no indemnity at all, and the insertion is a concise single-paragraph clause with no hold-harmless wording, no extra indemnitees, no settlement-consent proviso and no fallback remedy boilerplate.

Intent preserved: paragraphs 9(a) and 9(b) (including the Globix Agreement carve-out) are untouched, the new text uses only existing defined terms (Site, Services, Content, Confidential Information), and no dangling mechanic or contradiction is introduced.
